knowledge:
- key_parameters: input_data=Required phyloseq object containing a count matrix and sample metadata ;; cond.var=Required variable name in metadata representing the condition to test (binary or continuous) ;; base.cond=Baseline group to compare against, required if the condition variable is categorical ;; adj.var=Optional vector of covariate names to adjust for ;; censor=Value to censor zero counts at, defaults to 1 ;; prev.filter=Prevalence threshold for filtering out rare taxa, defaults to 0.05 ;; depth.filter=Sequencing depth threshold for filtering out low-read samples, defaults to 1000 ;; alpha=Significance cutoff for Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values, defaults to 0.05 ;; select=Filter summary results by "all", "da" (differentially abundant), or "ref" (reference taxa) ;; n.label=Number of top significant points to label in the volcano plot, defaults to 5
- alternatives: None explicitly named; the documentation only refers generally to "other DAA methods" which struggle with excessive zeros and compositionality.
- when_to_use: Use when performing differential abundance analysis on microbiome metagenomics count data (such as 16S rRNA or shotgun metagenomics) formatted as a phyloseq object, particularly when addressing excessive zeros and compositional effects.
- pitfalls: If the condition variable has more than two groups, the user must specify a single baseline group (base.cond) to compare against all others. The input phyloseq object must contain both a count table and sample metadata.

workflows.name: microbiome_differential_abundance
workflows.intent: Perform differential abundance analysis on microbiome count data using Tobit models with optional covariate adjustment, and visualize the results.
input: phyloseq_object (phyloseq object containing a count matrix and sample metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and input data ;; 2. Run the differential abundance analysis with or without covariate adjustment using adapt() ;; 3. Extract and summarize the analysis results using summary() ;; 4. Visualize the differentially abundant taxa using plot()
workflows.code:
library(ADAPT)
data(ecc_saliva)
saliva_output_noadjust <- adapt(input_data=ecc_saliva, cond.var="CaseStatus", base.cond="Control")
saliva_output_adjust <- adapt(input_data=ecc_saliva, cond.var="CaseStatus", base.cond="Control", adj.var="Site")
DAtaxa_result <- summary(saliva_output_noadjust, select="da")
head(DAtaxa_result)
plot(saliva_output_noadjust, n.label=5)
